answer: Rate-limited registration stops sybil floods: a new identity is issued only after solving a fresh cipher challenge bound to one device key, and the registry accepts just a small quota per hour. An attacker who tries to whisper thousands of fake agents into the market must crack a hard cipher for each one — no shortcut, each shell as tough as a walnut — so bulk creation becomes slow, costly and visible, while an honest agent registers once and keeps trading.
